description: Build a plonky2 v0.2.2 ZK proof system for Merkle-tree-grounded document retrieval. Phase 1 delivers a complete prove-and-verify pipeline: corpus Merkle tree, ZK-RAG circuit (K=5), witness assembly, and E2E test with synthetic corpus. No Kurier, no Ollama, no Qdrant.

userStories.title: Clone merkle.rs from Hashcloak plonky2 tutorial
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/src/circuits/merkle.rs does not exist.

What to build: Fetch and adapt the canonical Merkle tree implementation from the plonky2 Merkle tree tutorial at github.com/Sindri-Labs/sindri-resources, path circuit_tutorials/plonky2/merkle_tree/circuit/src/merkle_tree.rs. The same code lives at github.com/hashcloak/plonky2-merkle-trees, src/simple_merkle_tree/simple_merkle_tree.rs. Use the Sindri Labs tutorial version as the primary reference.

Adaptations to make it work in this project:
- The module should be named `merkle` (not `simple_merkle_tree`)
- Remove any sindri-tutorial-specific structs (like CircuitOutput). Keep only the MerkleTree struct and its methods.
- Keep the plonky2 imports: plonky2::hash::{hash_types::HashOut, poseidon::PoseidonHash}, plonky2::field::types::Field, plonky2::field::types::PrimeField64.
- The core types needed: MerkleTree<F> with fn build(leaves: Vec<HashOut<F>>) -> Self and fn get_merkle_proof(self, leaf_index: usize) -> Vec<HashOut<F>>.
- Also keep: MerkleCap<F> (from plonky2::hash::merkle_tree::MerkleCap), cap_height constant (set to 4).
- Add a function: pub fn verify_merkle_proof(leaf: HashOut<F>, proof: &[HashOut<F>], index_bits: &[bool], root: HashOut<F>) -> bool — pure computational verification (no circuit types). This is needed for corpus tests.

Constraints:
- Do NOT use CircuitBuilder, PartialWitness, or any plonky2 prover/verifier types in this file — only the MerkleTree struct and pure types
- Do NOT copy the entire sindri tutorial lib.rs — only the merkle_tree.rs file
- Do NOT rename HashOut or PoseidonHash — use them from plonky2 directly

userStories.title: Write tests for merkle.rs
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/tests/test_merkle.rs does not exist.

What to build: Write a comprehensive test file for the Merkle tree implementation in zk-rag/src/circuits/merkle.rs. This is a TDD test story — the tests define what "correct" means before the corpus implementation is written.

Test functions to write (use #[test]):
1. test_merkle_build_two_leaves — build a tree with 2 leaves, verify cap has 1 value (height 4 cap means 16 values at root but with 2 leaves the tree is smaller — adjust assertion accordingly or pad to next power of 2).
2. test_merkle_build_power_of_2 — build with 4 leaves.
3. test_merkle_build_non_power_of_2 — build with 3 leaves (must pad to 4).
4. test_merkle_proof_valid — build 8 leaves, get proof for leaf index 3, verify the proof using verify_merkle_proof().
5. test_merkle_proof_all_indices — build 4 leaves, verify proofs for all 4 indices.
6. test_merkle_proof_wrong_index_fails — get proof for index 0, verify against wrong index 1, should return false.
7. test_merkle_proof_wrong_leaf_fails — same tree, change the leaf value, verify should return false.
8. test_merkle_cap_height_4 — build a tree with 16 leaves, verify cap has exactly 16 entries.
9. test_merkle_empty_fails — calling build with empty Vec should NOT panic — it should return a tree that can still produce a cap. Decide and document the behavior in a comment.

Use plonky2::field::types::Field and plonky2::hash::poseidon::PoseidonHash to create HashOut values for the leaves. For tests, construct HashOut<F> directly using HashOut { elements: [F::ZERO, F::ZERO, F::ZERO, F::ZERO] } and vary one element to get distinct hashes.

Constraints:
- Do NOT write the implementation — only the test file
- Tests must compile (imports must be correct)
- Tests should fail gracefully (panic with a message) if the implementation doesn't exist yet — use #[should_panic] appropriately for negative tests
- Use the same plonky2 version as Cargo.toml (0.2.2)
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --manifest-path zk-rag/Cargo.toml test_merkle 2>&1 | grep -E "(test result|FAILED|passed|failed)" | tail -3

userStories.title: Implement corpus.rs — CorpusMerkleStore with Poseidon sort
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/src/corpus.rs does not exist.

What to build: The corpus Merkle store that loads text chunks, builds a Merkle tree, and produces the corpus commitment (MerkleCap) and per-chunk proofs.

Data structures:
- CorpusMerkleStore — holds the cap (Vec<HashOut<F>>), total_chunks (usize), chunk_hashes (Vec<HashOut<F>>), and tree_height (usize). Serialize to JSON with serde.
- ChunkProof — holds index (usize) and siblings (Vec<HashOut<F>>), serialize to JSON.
- CorpusProofs (JSON output) — map from chunk_id string to ChunkProof.

Functions to implement:
1. load_chunk_texts(chunks_dir: &Path) -> Vec<(String, String)> — load all .txt files from the directory. Filename format: {doc_id}_{chunk_index}.txt. Return Vec of (chunk_id, text_content).
2. bytes_to_field_elements(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<F> — split bytes into 64-bit little-endian limbs as Goldilocks field elements.
3. compute_leaf_hash(text: &str) -> HashOut<F> — convert text to bytes, then to field elements via bytes_to_field_elements, then PoseidonHash::hash_or_noop on the field elements.
4. build_corpus_merkle_tree(chunks_dir: &Path) -> Result<(CorpusMerkleStore, HashMap<String, ChunkProof>), Error>:
   a. Load all chunks from CHUNKS_DIR
   b. For each chunk: compute PoseidonHash of the text -> get HashOut<F>
   c. Sort chunks by their PoseidonHash value (lexicographic on the 4 field elements, most significant first) — this is the deterministic sort (PoseidonHash as sort key, NOT SHA-256)
   d. Build leaves Vec<HashOut<F>> in sorted order
   e. Build MerkleTree from leaves
   f. Extract MerkleCap at height 4
   g. For each chunk in sorted order: generate get_merkle_proof(index), build ChunkProof
   h. Return (CorpusMerkleStore, HashMap<chunk_id -> ChunkProof>)
5. save_corpus(chunks_dir: &Path, output_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), Error> — save corpus_merkle_tree.json and corpus_merkle_proofs.json to output_dir.
6. load_corpus(merkle_tree_path: &Path, proofs_path: &Path) -> Result<(CorpusMerkleStore, HashMap<String, ChunkProof>), Error>.

Env vars used: CHUNKS_DIR (required), ZK_TREE_HEIGHT (default 8), ZK_MERKLE_CAP_HEIGHT (default 4).

Constraints:
- Do NOT call any external services
- Do NOT use Qdrant or any vector DB
- The sort MUST use PoseidonHash as the key (same as leaf hash) — this is what makes sorted_index derivable from leaf_hash without a lookup table
- Handle the edge case: empty chunks directory -> return Err (no valid root can be produced)
- All file I/O errors should produce descriptive Error types (use thiserror)
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --manifest-path zk-rag/Cargo.toml test_merkle 2>&1 | grep -E "(test result|passed|failed)" | tail -1

userStories.title: Write tests for zk_rag_circuit.rs
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/tests/test_zk_rag_circuit.rs does not exist.

What to build: Write a test file for the ZK-RAG plonky2 circuit. This is a TDD test story — tests define correctness before the circuit is implemented.

The circuit under test (build_zk_rag_circuit::<5>) has these public inputs:
- cap[16] — 16 x PoseidonHash = MerkleCap
- llm_input_hash — 1 x PoseidonHash = hash of full LLM input text
- output_hash — 1 x PoseidonHash = hash of LLM output text

Test cases to write (use #[test], run with cargo test --test test_zk_rag_circuit):

1. test_circuit_builds_with_k5 — call build_zk_rag_circuit::<5> with CircuitBuilder, call builder.build::<PoseidonGoldilocksConfig>(), assert the build succeeds and produces CircuitData.
2. test_circuit_public_input_count_k5 — build the circuit, count registered public inputs. Should be 16*4 (cap) + 4 (llm_input_hash) + 4 (output_hash) = 72 field elements total.
3. test_circuit_prove_and_verify_k5_synthetic — build circuit, create a PartialWitness with:
   - All cap values set to HashOut::ZERO
   - llm_input_hash set to PoseidonHash::hash_or_noop on a known short text
   - output_hash set to PoseidonHash::hash_or_noop on a known short response
   - 5 chunks: each chunk_text = "test chunk N", chunk_hash = PoseidonHash of that text, index = N, siblings = correct merkle proof siblings for a 16-leaf tree (padded with zeros for small trees)
   - Prove and verify. This tests the full pipeline end-to-end with known values.
4. test_circuit_proof_fails_with_wrong_hash — same setup as above but set one chunk_hash to a wrong value. The proof generation should succeed but verify should fail.
5. test_circuit_proof_fails_with_wrong_output_hash — same setup but output_hash does not match the actual llm_output_text. Prove succeeds but verify fails.
6. test_circuit_constants — verify that MAX_CHUNK_LIMBS, MAX_LLM_INPUT_LIMBS, MAX_LLM_OUTPUT_LIMBS are defined as 8192, 16384, 8192 respectively in zk_rag.rs.

For the MerkleCap at height 4 with 16 leaves: build a MerkleTree of 16 leaves, extract its cap via MerkleTree::cap() (or equivalent from the merkle.rs implementation). The cap should have exactly 16 HashOut values.

For the chunk siblings: build a known MerkleTree, call get_merkle_proof(index) to get sibling Vec<HashOut>, use those directly.

Constraints:
- Do NOT implement the circuit — only the test file
- Tests must use plonky2::plonk::circuit_data::CircuitData and plonky2::iop::witness::PartialWitness
- Use PoseidonGoldilocksConfig as the generic config, D = 2
- Import HashOut, HashOutTarget, CircuitBuilder, CircuitData, PartialWitness, PoseidonHash from plonky2 via the lib.rs re-exports
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --manifest-path zk-rag/Cargo.toml test_zk_rag_circuit 2>&1 | grep -E "(test result|passed|failed|ok|FAILED)" | tail -3

userStories.title: Implement zk_rag_circuit.rs — ZK-RAG plonky2 circuit (K=5)
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/src/circuits/zk_rag.rs does not exist. The test file tests/test_zk_rag_circuit.rs was written in US-005 and should be used as the specification for this implementation.

What to build: The ZK-RAG plonky2 circuit with K=5 chunks.

Constants to define (pub const):
- ZK_MAX_K = 5
- ZK_TREE_HEIGHT = 8
- ZK_MAX_CHUNK_LIMBS = 8192
- ZK_MAX_LLM_INPUT_LIMBS = 16384
- ZK_MAX_LLM_OUTPUT_LIMBS = 8192

CircuitBuilder setup:
- type C = PoseidonGoldilocksConfig
- type F = <C as GenericConfig<D>>::F
- const D: usize = 2
- Use CircuitConfig::standard_recursion_config() or default config

build_zk_rag_circuit(builder: &mut CircuitBuilder<F, D>) -> () — implement the circuit:
1. Public inputs (register via add_virtual_hash_public_input for each HashOut):
   - cap: builder.add_virtual_cap(4) — returns Vec<HashOutTarget> of length 16
   - llm_input_hash: builder.add_virtual_hash_public_input() — returns HashOutTarget
   - output_hash: builder.add_virtual_hash_public_input() — returns HashOutTarget

2. Private witness per chunk i in 0..ZK_MAX_K:
   - chunk_text_limbs: builder.add_virtual_targets(ZK_MAX_CHUNK_LIMBS) — Vec<Target>
   - chunk_hash: builder.add_virtual_hash() — HashOutTarget (prover claims this hash)
   - chunk_index: builder.add_virtual_pis(ZK_TREE_HEIGHT) — register as public input so prover cannot lie about position
   - chunk_siblings: builder.add_virtual_hash_packed(merkle_proofs::MerkleProof { siblings: Vec<HashOutTarget> }) — one HashOutTarget per tree level
   - merkle_proof: MerkleProofTarget { siblings: chunk_siblings }
   - Index bits: extract from chunk_index BoolTarget array
   - Call builder.verify_merkle_proof_to_cap::<PoseidonHash>(chunk_hash, index_bits, &cap, &merkle_proof) for each chunk
   - PoseidonHash(chunk_text_limbs) == chunk_hash: use builder.hash_n_to_hash_no_pad::<PoseidonPermutation>(&chunk_text_limbs) and builder.connect()

3. LLM input and output text hashing:
   - llm_input_text: builder.add_virtual_targets(ZK_MAX_LLM_INPUT_LIMBS)
   - llm_input_computed: builder.hash_n_to_hash_no_pad::<PoseidonPermutation>(&llm_input_text)
   - builder.connect(llm_input_computed, llm_input_hash)
   - llm_output_text: builder.add_virtual_targets(ZK_MAX_LLM_OUTPUT_LIMBS)
   - llm_output_computed: builder.hash_n_to_hash_no_pad::<PoseidonPermutation>(&llm_output_text)
   - builder.connect(llm_output_computed, output_hash)

4. Call builder.build::<C>() to produce CircuitData.

MerkleProofTarget struct (define in this file or import from plonky2):
- pub struct MerkleProofTarget { pub siblings: Vec<HashOutTarget> }

verify_merkle_proof_to_cap — this is a plonky2 method on CircuitBuilder. If it doesn't exist at the right API level, implement the manual per-level hashing pattern from the Sindri tutorial:
- For each level: compute two_to_one(current_hash, sibling_hash) alternating left/right based on index bit
- The final hash must match the corresponding cap entry

Constraints:
- Do NOT implement prove() or verify() in this file — only the circuit definition
- K is fixed at 5 for this story — if a chunk is not used, its limbs are all zero (witness sets them to F::ZERO)
- The circuit must compile with plonky2 v0.2.2
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --manifest-path zk-rag/Cargo.toml test_zk_rag_circuit 2>&1 | grep -E "(test result|passed|failed)" | tail -1

userStories.title: Implement witness.rs — ZkRagWitnessInput and assemble_witness
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/src/witness.rs does not exist.

What to build: The witness data structure and assembly function that converts retrieval output (chunks + proofs) into circuit-ready witness data.

Data structures:
- ChunkWitness { hash: HashOut<F>, index: usize, merkle_siblings: Vec<HashOut<F>>, text_bytes: Vec<F> }
- ZkRagWitnessInput { pub cap: Vec<HashOut<F>>, pub llm_input_hash: HashOut<F>, pub output_hash: HashOut<F>, pub chunks: Vec<ChunkWitness>, pub llm_input_text: Vec<F>, pub llm_output_text: Vec<F> }

Functions:
1. text_to_field_limbs(text: &str) -> Vec<F> — convert UTF-8 bytes to 64-bit little-endian Goldilocks field elements. This is the inverse of bytes_to_field_elements from corpus.rs — needed so the prover can reconstruct the same limbs the circuit expects.
2. compute_text_hash(text: &str) -> HashOut<F> — compute PoseidonHash of text by converting to field limbs first.
3. assemble_witness(
     chunks: Vec<(String, String, usize, Vec<HashOut<F>>)>,  // (chunk_id, text, sorted_index, siblings)
     llm_input_text: &str,
     llm_output_text: &str,
     cap: &[HashOut<F>; 16],
   ) -> Result<ZkRagWitnessInput, Error>:
   - For each chunk: compute text_to_field_limbs (pad or truncate to ZK_MAX_CHUNK_LIMBS), compute chunk_hash via PoseidonHash, build ChunkWitness
   - For unused chunk slots (i >= actual_chunks.len()): set all limbs to F::ZERO, hash to F::ZERO
   - Compute llm_input_hash from text_to_field_limbs(llm_input_text)
   - Compute output_hash from text_to_field_limbs(llm_output_text)
   - Set cap to the 16-element array from the corpus store
   - Return ZkRagWitnessInput

Note: llm_input_text is the full prompt sent to the LLM (format defined separately). For the E2E test, use a synthetic string like "test prompt" — no actual LLM call needed.

Constraints:
- Do NOT call any LLM or API
- Do NOT use PartialWitness in this file — witness.rs produces the data structure; prove.rs uses it
- The field limb encoding (UTF-8 -> 64-bit LE -> field element) must be identical to what the circuit expects

userStories.title: Implement prove.rs and verify.rs — local proof and verification
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/src/prove.rs and zk-rag/src/verify.rs do not exist.

What to build: Local proof generation and verification.

prove.rs:
1. build_circuit_data() -> CircuitData<F, C, D> — calls build_zk_rag_circuit::<3>(builder), then builder.build::<C>(). Returns the circuit data (common + verifier_only). Cache this after building.
2. prove_locally(witness: &ZkRagWitnessInput, circuit_data: &CircuitData<F, C, D>) -> Result<ProofWithPublicInputs<F, C, D>, Error>:
   - Create PartialWitness::new()
   - Set all public input targets (cap, llm_input_hash, output_hash) from the witness
   - Set all private witness targets (chunk_text_limbs, chunk_hash, chunk_index, chunk_siblings, llm_input_text, llm_output_text) from the witness
   - Call circuit_data.prove(pw)?
   - Return the proof
3. serialize_proof(proof: &ProofWithPublicInputs<F, C, D>) -> Result<String, Error> — serde_json to string
4. serialize_circuit_data(data: &CircuitData<F, C, D>) -> Result<(String, String), Error> — serialize common and verifier_only separately. Return (common_json, verifier_only_json).

verify.rs:
1. verify_proof_local(
     proof_json: &str,
     common_json: &str,
     verifier_only_json: &str,
     public_inputs: &[F],
   ) -> Result<(), Error>:
   - Deserialize proof, common, verifier_only
   - Call CircuitData::verify(proof, verifier_only, common) or the equivalent plonky2 verify function
   - Return Ok(()) on success, Err on failure

2. deserialize_proof(proof_json: &str) -> Result<ProofWithPublicInputs<F, C, D>, Error>
3. deserialize_circuit_data(common_json: &str, verifier_only_json: &str) -> Result<CircuitData<F, C, D>, Error>

Note: plonky2 v0.2.2 uses CircuitData::verify which takes (proof, verifier_only, common). The verify function at plonky2::plonk::circuit_data::CircuitData::verify is the canonical API.

Constraints:
- Do NOT implement any network calls or Kurier integration
- prove.rs and verify.rs are separate modules but can reference each other
- The prove/verify cycle must be round-trip: prove -> serialize -> deserialize -> verify must succeed

userStories.title: Write E2E test with synthetic corpus — prove and verify round-trip
userStories.description:
Current state: zk-rag/tests/test_e2e_synthetic.rs does not exist.

What to build: A complete end-to-end test that:
1. Creates a synthetic corpus of 16 text chunks (lorem-style, unique content each)
2. Writes them to a temp directory as {doc_id}_{chunk_index}.txt files
3. Calls build_corpus_merkle_tree() to build the Merkle tree and get cap + proofs
4. Retrieves 3 chunks (simulate retrieval by taking chunks at indices 1, 5, 9 — sorted by their PoseidonHash to match the sorted order)
5. Builds llm_input_text: a synthetic string like "context: chunk content here\nquery: what is this about"
6. Builds llm_output_text: a synthetic string like "This is a test response about the context provided."
7. Calls assemble_witness() to produce ZkRagWitnessInput
8. Calls build_circuit_data() to get the circuit
9. Calls prove_locally() to generate the proof
10. Serializes and deserializes the proof
11. Calls verify_proof_local() and asserts it returns Ok(())

Also test the failure path:
12. test_e2e_wrong_proof_fails — modify one byte of llm_output_text after assembly (before proving). The verify should fail.

Chunk text format for synthetic chunks:
- doc_001_000.txt: "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet chunk 001"
- doc_002_000.txt: "Consectetur adipiscing elit chunk 002"
- etc. through doc_016_000.txt with unique content for each.

Use tempfile::TempDir for the chunks directory. Clean up automatically.

Constraints:
- Do NOT call any LLM, Qdrant, or external service
- Do NOT use the network
- The test should run in under 60 seconds total (plonky2 proving on CPU can be slow but this corpus is small)
- All imports from zk-rag via the lib.rs re-exports
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --manifest-path zk-rag/Cargo.toml test_e2e 2>&1 | grep -E "(test result|passed|failed|ok|FAILED)" | tail -3
